Conditional Access
Conditional Access is the main policy engine in Microsoft Entra ID. As the security perimeter
now extends idx_b822d9c0 beyond the traditional boundaries, organizations need to use new identity-driven
measures to secure corporate resources. Conditional Access is Microsoft's Zero Trust policy
engine. It takes signals from various sources and then enforces policy decisions. In simplest

terms, Conditional Access policies can be defined as if-then statements. For example, if a user
wants to access their email, they must complete an MFA challenge. Using Conditional Access
administrators can help users be productive anywhere and anytime, while protecting the
organization's resources. Conditional Access policies are enforced after the user has been
authenticated.
The minimum license required to use Conditional Access is Microsoft Entra ID P1.
Conditional Access receives signals from a variety of sources before enforcing decisions as
shown in the following figure:
Figure 2.39: Conditional Access overview
Using Conditional Access policies, an administrator can define conditions under which a user
is granted or denied access to corporate resources based on their sign-in conditions. For
example, if a user is accessing a corporate resource from a company-managed laptop on a
trusted network location, they can be allowed access to the corporate resource. If they are
accessing a corporate resource from a company-managed laptop but from an untrusted
network location, they may be prompted for MFA before access is granted. However, if they are
accessing corporate resources from an airport kiosk, they can be completely denied access to
the corporate resources.
Using Conditional Access policies, you can define granular control over access to corporate
resources based on user and sign-in signals.
Following are the common signals that Conditional Access policy decisions are based on:
User or group: Policies can be applied to individual users or based on group
membership.
•

User location: Policies can be applied based on the user's network location.
Organizations can define a list of trusted locations like their corporate or VPN IP
address ranges to be excluded from policy.
Device: Various device states such as operating system version, patch level, and
compliance level can be taken into consideration while applying a policy.
Application: Conditional Access policies can be triggered depending on the
application or the corporate resource the user is attempting to access.
Based on idx_980ddee7 the above signals, one of the following decisions can be made:
Block access
Grant access
Grant access subject to user satisfying conditions like MFA, ensuring device
compliance, forcing password change, accepting terms of use, and so on
An administrator can create Conditional Access policies from the Microsoft Entra
administrator portal. The following are the steps:
Log in to https://entra.microsoft.com as a Conditional Access Administrator.
Navigate to Entra ID | Conditional Access.

This chapter explained the fundamental concepts of Microsoft Entra ID. You learned about

Implementing Microsoft Entra ID
A good identity infrastructure is essential for an enterprise, as it enables better security and
user productivity. When you design an identity infrastructure for your organization, you must
consider various factors like the current identity model, the future desired state, the security
strategy, and the regulatory landscape the organization is subject to. Microsoft Entra ID
supports various implementation methods. Organizations born in the cloud can run
completely in the idx_7ba059c0 cloud without having any on-premises Active Directory (AD) servers.
However, most organizations have a significant on-premises infrastructure that is required to
run their business. Such organizations can run Microsoft Entra ID in hybrid mode, where
objects from on-premises AD can synchronize to Microsoft Entra ID. Depending on the identity
model an organization chooses, there are various options to synchronize on-premises objects
to Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft Entra ID also offers robust methods like Administrative Units
and end user self-service options to decentralize user and group management. It has strong
built-in security controls which provide a baseline level of security for all organizations.
This chapter will cover:
Determining and implementing the right identity model
Managing users and groups in Microsoft Entra ID
Administrative units
End-user self service
Fundamental security settings
Determining the identity model

identity idx_a484b82e and hybrid identity. This will vary based on your organization's identity requirements,

Creating groups
With Microsoft Entra ID, you can use groups to make management of user accounts easier.
Using groups idx_d99fc986 enables administrators to grant permissions and assign licenses to groups rather
than individual users. You can also manage access to applications using groups. There are two
types of groups available in Microsoft Entra ID as follows:
Security: These groups are used to manage user access to shared resources.
Microsoft 365: These groups offer collaboration capabilities across shared mailboxes,
SharePoint sites, and more.
Group membership can be managed in three ways as follows:
Assigned: Administrators can add each individual user to groups.
Dynamic user: Using this method, administrators can use rules to dynamically assign
users to groups. For example, you could create a group for all users in the Legal
department. This is based on the users' Microsoft Entra ID attributes. Once created, all
users whose Department field in Microsoft Entra ID is Legal will be dynamically added
to this group. As and when the user's Entra ID attributes are updated, the group
membership is dynamically updated.
Dynamic device: Using this idx_5e786c5f group type, you can dynamically add or remove devices to
a group based on their attributes.
The steps to create a group are explained in Chapter 2, Fundamentals of Microsoft Entra ID, under
the Using role-assignable groups section.
Hybrid identity
In a hybrid identity model, user accounts are created in on-premises AD and are synchronized
to Microsoft idx_c15d279d Entra ID. Most user account changes flow from on-premises to Microsoft Entra ID.
When hybrid identity is implemented, the on-premises AD remains authoritative for account
information. This means that you will be performing administrative tasks on-premises and
changes will be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. Provisioning and synchronization idx_bda11381 are key
concepts in hybrid identity. Provisioning means idx_505e1424 creating, updating, and deleting an object
based on certain conditions. Synchronization means ensuring that on-premises identity
information matches that in the cloud.

Microsoft Entra ID supports the following types of provisioning:
HR-driven provisioning: It involves creating user accounts in Microsoft Entra ID
directly idx_4cce272d from a supported HR system. When a idx_53e97506 new employee joins a company, they are
entered into the HR system. When this happens, their ID is automatically created in the
Microsoft Entra ID tenant. It also supports employee attribute changes such as when
employees move across teams and their attributes such as manager name, department,
etc., are updated. When employees leave the organization and their account in the HR
system is terminated the same is updated in Microsoft Entra ID as well.
App provisioning: This idx_6b665240 process encompasses the idx_00e52ccf automated creation, lifecycle
management, and deprovisioning of user identities across cloud-based applications. It
ensures that users are granted appropriate access to the services required for their
roles, while also maintaining compliance and security standards. Common scenarios
include provisioning Microsoft Entra user accounts into third-party SaaS platforms
such as Dropbox, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and other enterprise applications.
Directory provisioning: This idx_9923e612 involves provisioning idx_227a75c0 from on-premises AD forests to
Microsoft Entra ID. This chapter will focus on directory provisioning using Microsoft
Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Connect cloud provisioning.
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is a service from Microsoft that synchronizes on-premises Active
Directory idx_3a6ccef1 and Microsoft Entra ID using Microsoft online services. A lightweight idx_42b2e611 agent acts as a
bridge between Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory and stores the configuration in
Microsoft Entra ID. The agent provides cloud sync and on-premises app provisioning
capabilities. It uses SCIM and provides the following benefits:
Synchronize multiple disconnected Active Directory forests to a single Microsoft Entra
tenant.
Simple installation using a lightweight provisioning agent.
Supports groups with up to 50,000 members. If you have groups that have more than
50,000 members you will have to use Microsoft Entra Connect Sync.
Multiple provisioning agents can be used to address high availability scenarios.
Deployment scenarios
Microsoft idx_35badb7d Entra Cloud Sync supports the following deployment scenarios:
Integrate a single Active Directory Forest with a single Microsoft Entra tenant.
Integrate multiple Active Directory forests with a single Microsoft Entra tenant.

There idx_250b490a are two key components of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync:
A provisioning agent: Built on the same server-side technology as Application Proxy

A provisioning service: This is the service responsible for updating changes to the

RemoteSigned.

Microsoft Entra ID Connect offers password hash synchronization, pass-through

Microsoft Entra Connect Synchronization services (Microsoft Entra Connect Sync) is the
main component idx_da68e42f of Microsoft Entra Connect. This is the service that idx_2c97297a synchronizes identity
data between on-premises AD and Cloud. This sync service consists of two components: the

Installation requirements

Authentication methods
There are idx_474662f1 various methods of enabling authentication when on-premises identities are
synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. Choosing the right authentication type is the first concern
for organizations wanting to move to the cloud. This is a very important decision because:
It is the first decision an organization will make when they plan to move to the cloud

Microsoft Entra Connect offers three authentication choices: password hash sync, pass-

Password hash sync
Password hash sync is the simplest method to enable authentication for on-premises Active
Directory idx_56b87193 objects in the cloud. In this method, password idx_40e7c0b0 hashes are synchronized to Microsoft
Entra ID. The users can use the same usernames and passwords for all on-premises and cloud
applications. It idx_0b3398e8 offers the following key advantages:
Requires the least amount of administrative effort in terms of deployment,

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 3 88
chunks.content:
infrastructure, and maintenance.
Advanced identity protection features like leaked credential reports are available only
with this method.
Provides business continuity. If your on-premises Active Directory infrastructure is not
available, the users will still be able to authenticate.
Password hash sync can be used as a fallback mechanism for the other two
authentication methods. If you have certain business requirements that are not met by
password hash sync, you can use one of the other two methods and use password hash
idx_e44670ab sync as a fallback method to continue providing authentication services to your end
users in case your on-premises infrastructure is unavailable.
It also enables leaked credentials detection for hybrid accounts. Microsoft works with
security researchers and law enforcement to find username/password pairs that are
publicly available. If such accounts are found, Microsoft Entra flags them as high risk.
The on-premises idx_2f8c00f1 Active Directory stores user passwords as an MD4 hash idx_829fe2b1 value of the original
password. This is the result of a hashing algorithm, which is a one-way mathematical function.
There is no way that a hashed value can be reversed to obtain the original password.
Microsoft Entra Connect sync extracts the password hash from Active Directory and applies
additional security to the hashed password before synchronizing it with Microsoft Entra ID.
The passwords are synchronized every two minutes, and this interval cannot be modified.
On the first run, all passwords of in-scope users are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. You
can use staged rollout to test user groups with capabilities like MFA, Conditional Access,
Identity Protection, and Identity Governance. The following figure shows how password hash
sync works between Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.

The following idx_208540f0 are some important considerations for password hash synchronization:
The plain-text passwords are never exposed to the password hash synchronization
agent or to Microsoft Entra ID.
The passwords are never stored in SQL. They are only processed in memory and then
sent to Microsoft Entra ID.
Users are authenticated against the passwords stored in Microsoft Entra and not on the
on-premises Active Directory.
Since the MD4 idx_6d4ec04f hash is not transmitted idx_ef58bbcd to Microsoft Entra ID, if the Microsoft Entra ID
password is stolen, it cannot be deciphered back to the original password stored in on-
premises Active Directory. This protects the passwords from pass-the-hash attacks.
For synchronized users, the on-premises Active Directory password complexity policies
override the password complexity policies in Microsoft Entra ID. Users created directly
in the cloud still get the Microsoft Entra ID password complexity policy.
For synchronized users, the password in Microsoft Entra ID is set to Never Expire. The
account expiry attribute is not synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID from on-premises
Active Directory. It is possible for users to log in to cloud services even if their on-
premises password has expired. It is recommended to use a PowerShell script, using
the Set ‑ ADUser cmdlet, that disables a user's Entra ID account once their on-premises
Active Directory account expires.

Pass-through authentication
This is an alternative to the password hash sync method offering the same benefits of users
being able idx_9acf19bd to use the same username and idx_b725f979 password for both on-premises and cloud services.
However, some organizations that want to enforce their own Active Directory security and
password policies can choose pass-through authentication. In this method, passwords remain
stored on the on-premises Active Directory. When the user tries to access an application,
Microsoft Entra ID sends the authentication request to the pass-through authentication agent.
The agent validates the user's password against Active Directory and if the password idx_7bd4a035 matches,
the user is allowed access. Pass-through authentication offers the following benefits:
Users can use the same username and password to access both on-premises and cloud
applications.
It is easy to deploy and administer. A simple lightweight agent is deployed.
On-premises passwords are never stored in the cloud in any form.
The agent makes only outbound connections from your network.
Administrators can enforce on-premises password policies.

Administrative units
Administrative units allow you to segment your organization into smaller blocks based on
location, department, business unit, etc. This allows specific administrators to manage only
members of idx_5b5079a7 that unit. For example, you could have separate admin units for Americas, EMEA,
and Asia. You can then assign separate admins to control access, manage users, and set policies
for those specific geographies.
It is important to note that a single object can be included in multiple administrative units
depending on its scope. In the above example, if the organization has further administrative
units for departments such as Marketing, Finance, and HR, a marketing user in EMEA could be
a member of two administrative units, that is, EMEA and Marketing.
To create admin units, you need a Microsoft Entra P1 license for each administrative unit
administrator.
Restricted management administrative units
In some scenarios, organizations might want to protect specific objects from modification by
anyone idx_12506d71 other than a specific set idx_48523539 of administrators. For example, you might want to protect the

assign them to a restricted management administrative unit and assign a separate
administrator to that admin unit.

administrative unit scope level can perform all actions related to users, devices, and security
